To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed ROBMS‐ GLMM can provide valid inference for both population‐averaged and individual effects, while allowing for time‐varying covariates.

we propose a robust marginally specified GLMM for longitudinal data and that the ROBMS-GLMM is robust to deviations from the assumed random effects distribution and to outlying observations in the response and the covariates.

our robust marginally‐specified generalized linear mixed model is a flexible, effective, and computationally efficient method for analyzing longitudinal data, especially when the random effects are correlated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of robust methods for the analysis of correlated data.
the construction of a robust methodology for analyzing longitudinal data that is applicable when the distribution of random effects is unknown and when the data are contaminated.
developing methods for the analysis of data from longitudinal studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the robust approach to generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) proposed here is a useful alternative to the nonrobust approach for longitudinal data.
our ROBMS‐ GLMM provides a robust and flexible approach to longitudinal data analysis.
robustness in this context is achieved through a judicious combination of a robustified estimating equation with a collection of weights that provide robustness against outliers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a robust approach to the estimation of the parameters of a generalized linear mixed model.
we have developed a methodology that is robust to both outliers in the response variable and covariates as well as deviations in the random effects distribution.
we have developed a robust version of the generalized linear mixed model that is able to handle both population‐averaged and individual specific inference.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the robust approach to longitudinal data analysis is a viable alternative to the nonrobust approach.
robust inference is possible in longitudinal analyses and that the ROBMS-GLMM can be a useful tool in this context.
, in the presence of outlying responses or time‐varying covariates, the ROBMS approach can be used as an effective tool for achieving valid inference.
